classification.difficultyReason: Optimise the allowable centre separation while independently enforcing both diameter bounds, distinguish which constraint controls, and justify that each resulting minimum is attainable.

content.prompt: Find the length of the diagonal of the smallest square that contains two tangent circles (touching at exactly one point), one of radius $r$ and the other of radius $R$.

answer.short:
$d=\max\!\left\{2\sqrt2\max(r,R),(1+\sqrt2)(r+R)\right\}$.

The square must fit each diameter as well as the separation of the tangent centres.
answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the square's side. Each centre is at least its radius from every side, so the horizontal and vertical separations of the centres are each at most $s-r-R$. Their distance is $r+R$ because the circles touch.
$$\begin{align*}(r+R)^2&\le 2(s-r-R)^2\\s&\ge r+R+\frac{r+R}{\sqrt2}.\end{align*}$$
The square must also satisfy $s\ge2r$ and $s\ge2R$. These bounds are attainable: use opposite permitted corner positions when the centre-separation bound controls; when a diameter controls, move the smaller circle's centre within its permitted square until the centre distance is $r+R$.
$$\begin{align*}s_{\min}&=\max\!\left\{2r,2R,\left(1+\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)(r+R)\right\}\\d&=\sqrt2s_{\min}\\d&=\max\!\left\{2\sqrt2\max(r,R),(1+\sqrt2)(r+R)\right\}.\end{align*}$$
